A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
A.text: A system consists of two identical spheres each of mass 1.5 kg and radius 50 cm at the end of light rod. The distance between the centres of the two spheres is 5 m. What will be the moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the rod passing through its midpoint?
A.sol_text: Using parallel axis theorem: I = 2[I_cm + md^2]. For each sphere: I_cm = (2/5)MR^2 = (2/5)(1.5)(0.5)^2 = 0.15 kg⋅m^2. Distance from midpoint to each sphere center: d = 2.5 m. I = 2[(2/5)(1.5)(0.5)^2 + (1.5)(2.5)^2] = 2[0.15 + 9.375] = 2[9.525] = 19.05 kg⋅m^2

A.subject: Physics
A.text: If RE be the radius of Earth, then the ratio between the acceleration due to gravity at a depth 'r' below an height 'h' above the earth surface is:
A.sol_text: Acceleration due to gravity at r distance above the surface = GM/(R+r)^2. Acceleration due to gravity at r distance below the surface = GM/R^3 * (R-r). So, ratio = [(R-r)(R+r)^2]/R^3 = (R-r)(R^2+r^2+2Rr)/R^3 = 1 + r/RE - r^2/RE^2 - r^3/RE^3

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Consider two separate ideal gases of electrons and protons having same number of particles. The temperature of both the gases are same. The ratio of the uncertainty in determining the position of an electron to that of a proton is proportional to:
A.sol_text: Using Heisenberg uncertainty principle: Δx·Δp ≥ h. For thermal motion, Δp ~ m·v ~ sqrt(m·k_B·T). Therefore Δx ~ h/(sqrt(m·k_B·T)) ~ 1/sqrt(m). Since both gases are at same temperature with same number of particles, the ratio of uncertainties in position is: Δx_e/Δx_p ~ sqrt(m_p/m_e)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two thin metallic spherical shells of radii r1 and r2 (r1 < r2) are placed with their centres coinciding. A material of thermal conductivity K is filled in the space between the shells. The inner shell is maintained at temperature theta1 and the outer shell at temperature theta2(theta1<theta2). The rate at which heat flows radially through the material is :
A.sol_text: For heat conduction through a spherical shell, the thermal resistance is R = (r2 - r1)/(4*pi*K*r1*r2). The rate of heat flow is given by Q = delta_T/R = K*(theta2 - theta1)*(r2 - r1)/(4*pi*r1*r2) multiplied by 4*pi*r1*r2 = 4*pi*K*r1*r2*(theta2 - theta1)/(r2 - r1). The correct answer is (D).

A.subject: Physics
A.text: For a body executing S.H.M.: (a) Potential energy is always equal to its K.E. (B) Average potential and kinetic energy over any given time interval are always equal. (c) Sum of the kinetic and potential energy at any point of time is constant. (d) Average K.E. in one time period is equal to average potential energy in one time period. Choose the most appropriate option from the options given below.
A.sol_text: In S.H.M., sum of kinetic and potential energy will be constant and average kinetic energy and average potential energy over a complete time period are always equal. Statement (c) is true because total mechanical energy is conserved in S.H.M. Statement (d) is true because by energy conservation, average K.E. over one complete period equals average P.E. over one complete period, both equal to E/2 where E is total energy.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The equivalent resistance of the given circuit between the terminals A and B is:
A.sol_text: Since 5Ω is connected across conductor (between the same two points), we can remove it as it carries no current. R_eq = 1Ω

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
A.text: If VA and VB are the input voltages (either 5V or 0V) and Vo is the output voltage then the two gates represented in the following circuit (A) and (B) are:
A.sol_text: Using the truth table provided: When A=0,B=0: Vo=0; When A=0,B=1: Vo=1; When A=1,B=0: Vo=1; When A=1,B=1: Vo=1. This corresponds to an OR gate for circuit (A). For circuit (B), analyzing the transistor configuration with pull-up resistor and npn transistor, when input is high the transistor conducts pulling output low, and when input is low the transistor is off and output goes high through pull-up resistor. This is a NOT gate. Therefore the answer is (B) OR and NOT Gate.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Four identical hollow cylindrical columns of mild steel support a big structure of mass 50 × 10^3 kg. The inner and outer radii are 50 cm and 100 cm respectively. Assuming uniform local distribution, calculate the compression strain of each column. [Use Y = 2.0 × 10^11 Pa, g = 9.8 m/s^2]
A.sol_text: Load of mass will be equally distributed among four columns, so force on each column will be 125 × 10^3 N. Cross section area of the column = π[(1)^2 - (0.5)^2] = 2.355 m^2. Using Young's modulus: ε = F/(AY) = (125 × 10^3)/(2.355 × 2 × 10^11) = 2.65 × 10^-7

A.subject: Physics
A.text: If velocity [V], time [T] and force [F] are chosen as the base quantities, the dimensions of the mass will be:
A.sol_text: Using F = ma = m(dv/dt), we get m = F/(dv/dt). Since dv/dt has dimensions of [V T^(-1)], we have m = F/[V T^(-1)] = [F T V^(-1)]

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The magnetic field vector of an electromagnetic wave is given by B = B_0 * (i + j)/sqrt(2) * cos(kz - ωt), where i,j represents unit vector along x and y axis respectively. At t = 0 s, two electric charges q1 of 4π coulomb and q2 of 2π coulomb located at (0, 0, 3π/k) and (0, 0, 3π/k) respectively, have the same velocity of 0.5 c (where c is the velocity of light). The ratio of the force acting on charge q1 to q2 is:
A.sol_text: Force on q1: F_q1 = q(V × B) = 4π(0.5c) × B_0/sqrt(2) (cos(kz - ωt)i + cos(kz - ωt)j) = 4π(0.5c)(B_0/sqrt(2))cos(3π)k. Force on q2: F_q2 = q(V × B) = 2π(0.5c) × B_0/sqrt(2) (cos(kz - ωt)i + cos(kz - ωt)j) = 2π(0.5c)(B_0/sqrt(2))cos(3π)k. Ratio F_q1/F_q2 = 4π(0.5c) / 2π(0.5c) = 2:1

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen has volume 500 cm^3, temperature 300 K, pressure 400 kPa and mass 0.76 g. The ratio of masses of oxygen to hydrogen will be:
A.sol_text: Using Ideal gas Equation PV = nRT: n = PV/(RT) = (400 × 10^3 × 500 × 10^(-6))/(8.3 × 300) = 0.008 mol. Let m_H = mass of hydrogen, m_O = mass of oxygen. Then m_H/2 + m_O/32 = 0.08 and 16m_H + m_O = 2.56. Solving: 16m_H + 0.76 - m_H = 2.56, which gives m_H = 0.12 m and m_O = 0.64. Therefore m_O/m_H = 0.64/0.12 = 16/3.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Statement-I: If three forces F1, F2, and F3 are represented by three sides of a triangle and, F1 + F2 = -F3, then these three forces are concurrent forces and satisfy the condition for equilibrium. Statement-II: A triangle made up of three forces F1, F2, and F3 as its sides taken in the same order, satisfy the condition for translatory equilibrium. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A free electron of 2.6 eV energy collides with a H+ ion. This results in the formation of a hydrogen atom in first excited state and a photon is released. Find the frequency of the emitted photon. (h = 6.6 × 10^(-34) Js)
A.sol_text: Energy of electron in first excited state will be -3.4eV. So total energy difference will be (2.6+3.4)eV = 6eV. Wavelength(λ) = 1242eV·nm / 6eV = 207 nm. Frequency = c/λ = (3×10^8) / (207×10^(-9)) = 1.45 × 10^15 Hz = 1.45 × 10^9 MHz

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A block moving horizontally on a smooth surface with a speed of 40 m/s splits into two parts with masses in the ratio 1:2. If the smaller part moves at 60 m/s in the same direction, then the fractional change in kinetic energy is:-
A.sol_text: Using conservation of linear momentum: 40 × 3m = 60 × m + v × 2m, which gives v = 30 m/s. Initial kinetic energy: KEi = (1/2) × 3m × (40)^2. Final kinetic energy: KEf = (1/2) × m × (60)^2 + (1/2) × 2m × (30)^2. Taking the ratio: KEf/KEi = 54/48. Fractional change in kinetic energy = 1 - KEf/KEi = 1 - 54/48 = -1/8, so the magnitude of fractional change is 1/8.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two forces (P + Q) and (P - Q) where P ⊥ Q, when act at an angle θ₁ to each other, the magnitude of their resultant is sqrt(3(P^2 + Q^2)), when they act at an angle θ₂, the magnitude of their resultant becomes sqrt(2(P^2 + Q^2)). This is possible only when θ₁ < θ₂. In the situation given above, θ₁ = 60° and θ₂ = 90°. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
A.sol_text: Let x = P + Q = sqrt(P^2 + Q^2) and y = P - Q = sqrt(P^2 + Q^2). Then |x + y| = sqrt(x^2 + y^2 + 2xy) = sqrt(3(P^2 + Q^2)), which gives θ₁ = 60°. Using the same formula for θ₂ = 90°, we get the resultant as sqrt(2(P^2 + Q^2)). This confirms that θ₁ = 60° and θ₂ = 90° are consistent with the given conditions, making both statements true.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A bob of mass 'm' suspended by a thread of length l undergoes simple harmonic oscillations with time period T. If the bob is immersed in a liquid that has density 1/4 times that of the bob and the length of the thread is increased by 1/3 of the original length, then the time period of the simple harmonic oscillations will be -
A.sol_text: Initial time period T = 2π*sqrt(l/g_eff). When bob is immersed in liquid with density 1/4 of bob's density, buoyant force acts upward. The effective gravity becomes g(1 - ρ_liquid/ρ_bob) = g(1 - 1/4) = 3g/4. New length l' = l + l/3 = 4l/3. New period T' = 2π*sqrt(l'/(g*3/4)) = 2π*sqrt((4l/3)/(3g/4)) = 2π*sqrt(16l/9g) = (4/3)*2π*sqrt(l/g) = (4/3)T

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A coil is placed in a magnetic field as shown below. B is a current induced in the coil because B is:
options: Parallel to the plane of coil and decreasing with time
Parallel to the plane of coil and increasing with time
A.sol_text: By Lenz's law, the induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux. The diagram shows an induced current in the coil. The direction of the induced current (shown as red arrow) indicates that the magnetic field through the coil must be changing. Using the right-hand rule and Lenz's law, if the induced current flows in the direction shown, it creates a magnetic field opposing the change in external field B. The induced current direction suggests that B is outward (perpendicular to the coil plane) and decreasing with time, so the induced current opposes this decrease.

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
A.text: Statement-I: To get a steady dc output from the pulsating voltage received from a full wave rectifier we can connect a capacitor across the output parallel to the load RL. Statement-II: To get a steady dc output from the pulsating voltage received from a full wave rectifier we can connect an inductor in series with RL. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A current of 1.5 A is flowing through a triangle, of side 9 cm each. The magnetic field at the centroid of the triangle is ___. (Assume that the current is flowing in the clockwise direction.)
options: 2√3 × 10^-7 T, outside the plane of triangle
2√3 × 10^-8 T, inside the plane of triangle
3 × 10^-5 T, inside the plane of triangle
3 × 10^-7 T, outside the plane of triangle
A.sol_text: Using magnetic field due to straight wire: B = (μ₀I)/(4πr) × (sin α + sin β). For an equilateral triangle with side 9 cm, the perpendicular distance from centroid to each side is r = 9/(2√3) cm = 0.09/(2√3) m. For each side, α = β = 60°. B = (10^-7 × 1.5)/(0.09/(2√3)) × (sin 60° + sin 60°) = 10^-5 T. Magnetic field due to three wires = 3 × 10^-5 T. Using right-hand rule with clockwise current, field is inside the plane of triangle.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Choose the incorrect statement: (a) The electric lines of force on a Gaussian surface provide negative flux. (b) A charge 'q' is placed at the centre of a cube. The flux through all the faces will be the same. (c) In a uniform electric field net flux through a closed Gaussian surface containing no net charge is zero. (d) When electric field is parallel to a Gaussian surface, it provides a finite non-zero flux. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
A.sol_text: When electric field is parallel to a Gaussian surface, it would provide zero flux. The dot product of E and dA is zero when they are perpendicular (field parallel to surface means perpendicular to normal). Statement (d) is incorrect as it claims finite non-zero flux. Statement (a) is also incorrect as electric field lines provide both positive and negative flux depending on direction - the sign of flux is not determined by the field lines alone but by the angle with surface normal.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A particle is moving with constant acceleration 'a'. Following graph shows v² versus x (displacement) plot. The acceleration of the particle is _____ m/s².
B.sol_text: From the graph, the equation of the line is v² = 2x + 20. Using the kinematic equation v² = u² + 2as, where u is initial velocity and a is acceleration. Comparing v² = 2x + 20 with v² = u² + 2as: 2a = 2, therefore a = 1 m/s². Also, u² = 20, so u = 2√5 m/s.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: The diameter of a spherical bob is measured using a vernier calipers. 9 divisions of the main scale, in vernier calipers, are equal to 10 divisions of vernier scale. One main scale division is 1 mm. The main scale reading is 10 mm and 8th division of vernier scale was found to coincide exactly with one of the main scale division. If the given vernier calipers has positive zero error of 0.04 cm, then the radius of the bob is ___ × 10^(-2) cm.
B.sol_text: LC = IMSD - 1VSD = 1MSD - (9/10)MSD = 0.1IMSD = 0.1 × 1 mm = 0.1 mm. Reading = 10 mm + 8 × 0.1 mm = 10.8 mm. Final reading = 10.8 mm - 0.04 mm = 10.4 mm = 104 × 10^(-2) cm. So radius = 50 × 10^(-2) cm.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A resistor dissipates 192 J of energy in 1 s when a current of 4A is passed through it. Now, when the current is doubled, the amount of thermal energy dissipated in 5 s is _____ J.
B.sol_text: Using Heat equation: H = i^2*R*t. From initial condition: 192 = (4)^2*R*(1), so R = 12 ohms. When current is doubled to 8A for time 5s: H = (8)^2*R*(5) = 64*12*5 = 3840 J
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A bandwidth of 6 MHz is available for A.M. transmission. If the maximum audio signal frequency used for modulating the carrier wave is not to exceed 6 kHz, the number of stations that can be broadcasted within this band simultaneously without interfering with each other will be ____.
B.sol_text: Signal bandwidth = 12 kHz. No. of station = 6 MHz / 12 kHz = 500
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A long solenoid with 1000 turns/m has a core material with relative permeability 500 and volume 10^3 cm^3. If the core material is replaced by another material having relative permeability of 750 with same volume maintaining same current of 0.75 A in the solenoid, the fractional change in the magnetic moment of the core would be approximately (x/499). Find the value of x.
B.sol_text: Magnetic moment M = (mu_r - 1) * (B/mu_0) * V = (mu_r - 1) * n * I * V, where n is turns per unit length. For initial material: M1 = (500 - 1) * 1000 * 0.75 * 10^(-3) = 499 * 0.75. For final material: M2 = (750 - 1) * 1000 * 0.75 * 10^(-3) = 749 * 0.75. Fractional change = (M2 - M1)/M1 = (749 - 499)/499 = 250/499. Therefore x = 250.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Identify correct A, B and C in the reaction sequence given below: Benzene + conc.HNO3 + conc.H2SO4 with heat gives A. A + Cl2 with Anhydrous AlCl3 gives B. B + Fe/HCl gives C.
options: A = Nitrobenzene, B = 2-Chloro-4-nitrochlorobenzene, C = 3-Chloroaniline with NH2
A = Nitrobenzene, B = 3-Chloronitrobenzene, C = 3-Aminophenol with NH2
A = Nitrobenzene, B = 4-Chloro-2-nitrochlorobenzene, C = 4-Chloroaniline with NH2 and Cl
A.sol_text: Step 1: Benzene undergoes nitration with conc.HNO3 and conc.H2SO4 under heat to form nitrobenzene (A). Step 2: Nitrobenzene (A) undergoes chlorination with Cl2 and anhydrous AlCl3 (Friedel-Crafts chlorination). Since NO2 is a deactivating group and meta-directing, chlorination occurs at the meta position to form 3-chloronitrobenzene (B). Step 3: 3-Chloronitrobenzene (B) is reduced with Fe/HCl. The NO2 group is reduced to NH2, and the C-Cl bond remains intact (as Cl is not reduced under these conditions), forming 3-chloroaniline (C).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Cell constant, (b) Molar conductivity, (c) Conductivity, (d) Degree of dissociation of electrolyte. List-II: (i) S cm^2 mol^(-1), (ii) Dimensionless, (iii) m^(-1), (iv) Ω^(-1) m^(-1). Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
A.sol_text: Matching parameters with their units/properties: (a) Cell constant = l/A, units are m/m^2 = m^(-1), so matches (iii). (b) Molar conductivity (λm) = κ × 1000/molarity, units are S cm^2 mol^(-1), so matches (i). (c) Conductivity (κ) = 1/ρ = l/(RA), units are Ω^(-1) m^(-1), so matches (iv). (d) Degree of dissociation α = number of moles dissociated/total moles, dimensionless, so matches (ii). Therefore: (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: For following sequence of reactions, the correct products are: 1. Br2 / Fe / A 2. Mg / dry ether 3. CH3OH → Products
options: Benzene with Br substituent + Mg with OCH3 group
Toluene with CH3 + Mg with OH and Br
Benzene with H + Mg with OCH3 and Br
A.sol_text: Step 1: Benzene undergoes bromination with Br2/Fe to form bromobenzene (C6H5Br). Step 2: Bromobenzene reacts with Mg in dry ether to form phenylmagnesium bromide (C6H5MgBr), a Grignard reagent. Step 3: The Grignard reagent reacts with CH3OH (methanol) to undergo protonolysis, where the C-Mg bond is replaced by C-H, forming benzene and magnesium methoxide (MgBr(OCH3)). The products are benzene with H and Mg complex with OCH3 and Br groups.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which one of the following correctly represents the order of stability of oxides X2O? (X = halogen)
A.sol_text: Stability order of oxides (X2O) is: I2O > Cl2O > Br2O. Bonds of halogen & oxygen are covalent due to less EN difference. Stability of (Cl-O) bond is higher due to its polarity and that of (I-O) bond is higher due to better overlap of orbitals. Therefore, the order is I > Cl > Br.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: Arrange the following conformational isomers of n-butane in order of their increasing potential energy
A.sol_text: Structure (I) is anti conformer - most stable, lowest energy. Structure (II) is fully eclipsed conformer - highest energy. Structure (III) is skew or gauche conformer - intermediate energy. Structure (IV) is partially eclipsed - intermediate energy but higher than gauche. Order of stability: (I) > (III) > (IV) > (II). Therefore order of increasing potential energy: I < III < IV < II

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The Eu^2+ ion is a strong reducing agent in spite of its ground state electronic configuration (outermost). [Atomic number of Eu = 63]. What is the electronic configuration of Eu^2+?
A.sol_text: Eu (Z = 63) has ground state configuration [Xe]4f^7 6s^2. Eu^2+ (Z = 63) loses 2 electrons to form [Xe]4f^7. Eu^3+ in spite of having 4f^6 configuration is strong reducing agent as it changes to most common oxidation state which is +3. Also, E(Eu^2+/Eu^3+) is low that is -2V.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: For the reaction given below: A benzene ring with CHO at top and CH2OH at bottom, treated with 1. NaOH, Δ 2. H3O+ gives Product. The compound which is not formed as a product in the reaction is a:
options: compound with both alcohol and acid functional groups
A.sol_text: The starting material has CHO (aldehyde) and CH2OH (primary alcohol) groups on a benzene ring. Under basic conditions (NaOH, heat), the aldehyde undergoes Cannizzaro reaction since there is no alpha hydrogen. The aldehyde is oxidized to carboxylate (COO- Na+) and the CH2OH is reduced further. Upon acidification with H3O+, the carboxylate becomes COOH. The products formed are: 1) A monocarboxylic acid (from the CHO group becoming COOH with CH2OH intact), 2) A diol with two CH2OH groups (from the other molecule in Cannizzaro). The compound not formed is a dicarboxylic acid, as only one aldehyde group is oxidized to carboxylic acid. The answer is (A) dicarboxylic acid.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of fibrous protein?
A.sol_text: Albumin is not an example of fibrous protein but globular protein. Keratin, myosin, and collagen are all fibrous proteins. Albumin is a globular protein found in blood plasma.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Spin only magnetic moment in BM of [Fe(CO)x(C6O4)]^+ is:
A.sol_text: For [Fe(CO)x(C6O4)]^+: First determine x from charge balance: x + 4(0) - 2(x) = +1, so x = -3. Fe^3+ has electronic configuration 4s^0 3d^5. In presence of strong ligand CO, the 3d electrons pair up: (↑↓)(↑↓)(↑)(↑↑)(↑↑) with d^5sp^3 hybridization. This gives 1 unpaired electron. Spin only magnetic moment = sqrt(n(n+2))BM = sqrt(1(1+2))BM = sqrt(3)BM = 1.73BM

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The incorrect expression among the following is:
A.sol_text: The solution shows derivations for thermodynamic relationships. (a) Derives ΔG = ΔG° + RT lnQ, then ΔG° = -RT lnK_eq and ΔH° - TAS° = -RT lnK_eq, giving lnK_eq = -(ΔH° - TAS°)/RT. (b) Shows W_rev = -nRT ln(V_f/V_i) for isothermal process. (c) Shows ΔG = -TAS_total at constant P, therefore ΔG/ΔS_total = -T. (d) Shows ΔG° = -RT lnK_eq. Option (A) has incorrect form - it should be lnK_eq = -(ΔH° - TAS°)/RT, not ink = (ΔH° - TAS°)/RT. The correct answer is (A).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The structures of A and B formed in the following reaction are: [Ph = -C6H5]. Benzene + phthalic anhydride reacted with AlCl3 (2eq) gives A, then Zn/Hg and HCl gives B
options: A = Ph-C(=O)-C(=O)-Ph with two phenyl groups, B = Ph-CH2-CH2-Ph
A = Ph-C(=O)-C(=O)-Ph with two phenyl groups, B = Ph-CH(OH)-CH2-Ph
A.sol_text: Phthalic anhydride reacts with benzene in presence of AlCl3 (Friedel-Crafts acylation) to form A, which is a diketone with formula containing Ph-C(=O) groups. Treatment with Zn/Hg and HCl (Clemmensen reduction) reduces the carbonyl groups to CH2 groups to form B. The correct answer is (D) where A is the diketo compound with carboxylic acid moiety and B is the corresponding reduced product with primary alcohol.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which among the following is not a polyester?
A.sol_text: Glyptal, Dacron & PHBV are polyesters. Novolac is a copolymer of phenol & formaldehyde but not a polyester.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Mn^2+, (b) As^3+, (c) Cu^2+, (d) Al^3+. List-II: (i) Group - III, (ii) Group - IIA, (iii) Group - IV, (iv) Group - IIB. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
A.sol_text: Based on qualitative analysis grouping: Mn^2+ belongs to Group IV (reduces with H2S, Co^2+, Zn^2+, Ni^2+); As^3+ belongs to Group IIB (As^3+, As^5+, Sb^3+, Sb^5+, Sn^2+, Sn^4+); Cu^2+ belongs to Group IIA (Cu^2+, Pb^2+, Hg^2+, Cd^2+, Bi^3+); Al^3+ belongs to Group III (Fe^3+, Al^3+, Cr^3+). Matching: (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The deposition of X and Y on ground surfaces is referred as wet and dry depositions, respectively. X and Y are:
A.sol_text: Wet deposition involves ammonium salts in rain drops forming NH4OH. Dry deposition involves oxides of N and S (like SO2) settling on ground. Therefore X = Ammonium salts (wet deposition) and Y = SO2 (dry deposition).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The major products A and B formed in the following reaction sequence are: Aniline reacted with acetic anhydride to form product A, which is then treated with Br2/CH3COOH at room temperature to form product B.
options: A = N-phenylacetamide with amino and methoxy groups, B = dibrominated product with amino and methoxy groups
A = N-phenylacetamide with amino and methoxy groups, B = monobrominated product with amino and methoxy groups
A.sol_text: Aniline (NH2-C6H5) reacts with acetic anhydride to form N-phenylacetamide (A = HN-C(=O)-CH3 attached to benzene). The N-phenylacetamide undergoes electrophilic aromatic bromination with Br2/CH3COOH. The acetamido group (-NH-C(=O)-CH3) is an ortho/para directing group and weakly deactivating. Bromination occurs at the para position (and ortho position) relative to the acetamido group, giving 4-bromo-N-phenylacetamide as the major product (B). Therefore A = N-phenylacetamide and B = 4-bromo-N-phenylacetamide.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The number of S=O bonds present in sulphurous acid, peroxodisulphuric acid and pyrosulphuric acid, respectively are:
A.sol_text: Sulphurous acid H2SO3 has 1 S=O bond. Peroxodisulphuric acid H2S2O8 has 4 S=O bonds. Pyrosulphuric acid H2S2O7 has 3 S=O bonds. Therefore the answer is 1, 4 and 3.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The major product of the following reaction is: A cyclopentene ring with CH3 group at top and Cl group on the right side, reacted with NaOH in C2H5OH solvent to give Major Product
options: A cyclopentene ring with CH3 at top and OH group below
A cyclopentene ring with CH3 as a substituent on the ring
A cyclopentene ring with CH3 and OH groups as substituents
A cyclopentene ring with CH3 at top and OH group as substituent
A.sol_text: This is an elimination reaction. The substrate is a cyclopentene derivative with CH3 and Cl groups. When treated with NaOH in ethanol (C2H5OH), which is a strong base and good nucleophile in polar protic solvent, an E2 elimination mechanism occurs preferentially over substitution (SN2). The Cl acts as leaving group and a beta-hydrogen is abstracted by the base, forming a double bond. The major product follows Zaitsev's rule - the most substituted alkene is formed. The CH3 group can shift (Wagner-Meerwein rearrangement) or the double bond forms in the most stable position. Option (B) shows the cyclopentene with CH3 substituent, which is the result of the elimination reaction forming the most stable alkene product.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which one of the following statements is incorrect? (A) Atomic hydrogen is produced when H2 molecules at a high temperature are irradiated with UV radiation. (B) Bond dissociation enthalpy of H2 is highest among diatomic gaseous molecules which contain a single bond. (C) Dihydrogen is produced on reacting zinc with HCl as well as with NaOH(aq). (D) At around 2000 K, the dissociation of dihydrogen into its atoms is nearly 8.1%.
options: Atomic hydrogen is produced when H2 molecules at a high temperature are irradiated with UV radiation.
Bond dissociation enthalpy of H2 is highest among diatomic gaseous molecules which contain a single bond.
Dihydrogen is produced on reacting zinc with HCl as well as with NaOH(aq).
At around 2000 K, the dissociation of dihydrogen into its atoms is nearly 8.1%.
A.sol_text: The solution shows various reactions: H2 with high temperature (hv) produces 2H; Zn + 2HCl produces ZnCl2 + H2; NaOH(aq) + Zn produces Na2ZnO2 + H2; H2 at 2000K produces 2H with dissociation of nearly 0.081%. Statement (D) is incorrect because the dissociation is nearly 0.081%, not 8.1%.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: In which one of the following sets all species show disproportionation reaction?
A.sol_text: ClO2, Cl2, Mn3+ can show disproportionation reaction while MnO2 cannot show disproportionation reaction. For disproportionation, an element must have an intermediate oxidation state so it can both increase and decrease. ClO2, Cl2, Mn3+ have intermediate oxidation states that allow disproportionation, but MnO2 with Mn in +4 state cannot undergo disproportionation.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Lithium salts are hydrated. Reason (R): Lithium has higher polarising power than other alkali metal group members. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
A.sol_text: Lithium salts are extensively hydrated due to high hydration enthalpy of Li+ ion. The polarising power order is: Li+ > Na+ > K+ > Rb+ > Cs+. Both assertion and reason are correct. The high polarising power of Li+ causes strong polarisation of water molecules, leading to extensive hydration. Therefore, reason R is the correct explanation for assertion A.

B.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
B.text: The transformation occurring in Duma's method is given below: C6H5N + (2x + y/2)CuO → xCO2 + y/2 H2O + z/2 N2 + (2x + y/2)Cu. The value of y is _______. (Integer answer)
B.sol_text: Using the given equation: C6H5N + (2x + y/2)CuO → xCO2 + y/2 H2O + z/2 N2 + (2x + y/2)Cu. Balancing atoms: For C: 6 = x, so x = 6. For H: 5 = y, so y = 10. For N: 1 = z/2, so z = 2. Substituting x = 6: (2×6 + 7) = 19 on both sides. By balancing the equation with x = 6, we get y = 7.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: The pH of a solution obtained by mixing 50 mL of 1 M HCl and 30 mL of 1 M NaOH is x × 10^(-4). The value of x is ________. (Nearest integer) [log 2.5 = 0.3979]
B.sol_text: Initial moles: HCl = 50 × 1/1000 = 0.05 mol, NaOH = 30 × 1/1000 = 0.03 mol. After reaction: HCl remaining = 0.05 - 0.03 = 0.02 mol, NaOH remaining = 0 mol. Total volume = 50 + 30 = 80 mL = 0.08 L. [H+] = 0.02/0.08 = 0.25 M = 2.5 × 10^(-1) M. pH = -log(2.5 × 10^(-1)) = -log(2.5) - log(10^(-1)) = -0.3979 + 1 = 0.6021. pOH = 14 - 0.6021 = 13.3979. [H+] = 10^(-0.6021) ≈ 2.5 × 10^(-1) M. For the acidic solution: pH = -log(0.25) = -log(2.5 × 10^(-1)) = 1 - 0.3979 = 0.6021. [H+] = 10^(-0.6021) = 2.5 × 10^(-1). Alternatively, [H+] = 0.02/0.08 = 1/4 = 0.25 = 2.5 × 10^(-1). Using pH = -log[H+] directly with given log value: x × 10^(-4) corresponds to the hydrogen ion concentration calculation. x = 6021 or approximately 6021.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: 1.22 g of an organic acid is separately dissolved in 100 g of benzene (Kb = 2.6 K kg mol^-1) and 100 g of acetone (Kb = 1.7 K kg mol^-1). The acid is known to dimerize in benzene but acts as a monomer in acetone. The boiling point of the solution in acetone increases by 0.17°C. The increase in boiling point of solution in benzene in °C is x × 10^-2. The value of x is ___ (Nearest integer) [Atomic mass: C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O = 16.0]
B.sol_text: For acetone solution: Using ΔTb = i × Kb × m, where i = 1 (monomer), calculate molar mass M = 122 g/mol. For benzene solution: The acid dimerizes (i = 1/2), so ΔTb = (1/2) × 2.6 × (1.22 × 1000)/(122 × 100) = 0.13°C = 13 × 10^-2 °C. Therefore x = 13.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: For the reaction A → B, the rate constant K(in s^(-1)) is given by log₁₀ K = 20.35 - (2.47×10³)/T. The energy of activation in kJ mol^(-1) is _____. (Nearest integer) [Given: R = 8.314 J K^(-1) mol^(-1)]
B.sol_text: Given: log₁₀ K = 20.35 - (2.47×10³)/T. Comparing with Arrhenius equation in logarithmic form: log K = log A - Ea/(2.303RT). We get Ea/(2.303R) = 2.47×10³. Therefore, Ea = (2.47×10³ × 2.303 × 8.314)/1000 = 47.29 kJ/mol ≈ 47 kJ/mol (nearest integer).
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.text: If dy/dx = x[y^2 + φ(y/x^2)] / [φ(y/x^2)], x > 0, φ > 0, and y(1) = -1, then φ(y^2/4) is equal to:
A.sol_text: Using substitution y/x = t, the differential equation is transformed. After simplification with u = φ(t^2), the equation becomes: (1/2)(du/u) = (1/x)dx, which integrates to (1/2)ln(u) = ln(x) + C. Using initial condition x=1, y=-1 to find C = (1/2)ln(φ(1)). The general solution is ln(φ(y^2/x^2)) = ln(x^2) + ln(φ(1)). At x=2: ln(φ(y^2/4)) = ln(4) + ln(φ(1)) = ln(4φ(1)). Therefore φ(y^2/4) = 4φ(1).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The number of solutions of the equation 32^(sin^2 x) + 32^(cos^2 x) = 81.0 <= x <= pi/4 is:
A.sol_text: Let 32^(sin^2 x) + 32^(cos^2 x) = 81. Since sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 1, let sin^2 x = t, then cos^2 x = 1-t. So 32^t + 32^(1-t) = 81. This gives 32^t + 32/32^t = 81. Multiply by 32^t: (32^t)^2 - 81(32^t) + 32 = 0. Let y = 32^t: y^2 - 81y + 32 = 0 gives y = 1 or y = 32. When 32^t = 1, t = 0 (so sin^2 x = 0, x = 0). When 32^t = 32, t = 1 (so sin^2 x = 1, but this is outside [0, pi/4]). For x in [0, pi/4], tan^2 x in [0,1]. Checking x = 0 gives one solution.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If α = lim(x→π/4) [tan^3(x) - tan(x)] / [cos(x + π/4)] and β = lim(x→0) [cos(x)]^(cot^2(x)) are the roots of the equation ax^2 + bx - 4 = 0, then the ordered pair (a, b) is:
A.sol_text: For α: Using L'Hôpital's rule and algebraic manipulation, α = lim(x→π/4) [3tan^2(x)·sec^2(x) - sec^2(x)] / [-sin(x + π/4)] = -4. For β: β = lim(x→0) [cos(x)]^(cot^2(x)) = e^(lim(x→0) cot^2(x)·ln(cos(x))) = e^(lim(x→0) -sin(x)/sec^2(x)) = e^0 = 1. The equation with roots α = -4 and β = 1 is x^2 + 3x - 4 = 0, giving a = 1, b = 3.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let a, b, c be three vectors mutually perpendicular to each other and have same magnitude. If a vector r satisfies a × ((r - b) × a) + b × ((r - c) × b) + c × ((r - a) × c) = 0, then r is equal to
A.sol_text: Given that a, b, c are mutually perpendicular vectors with equal magnitude |a| = |b| = |c|. Expanding the given equation a × ((r - b) × a) + b × ((r - c) × b) + c × ((r - a) × c) = 0 using vector triple product formula. After simplification using a · b = b · c = c · a = 0 and |a|² = |b|² = |c|², we get |a|²(3r - (a + b + c)) - (a·r)a - (b·r)b - (c·r)c = 0. Let r = xa + yb + zc. This leads to |a|²(2r - (a + b + c)) = 0, giving r = (a + b + c)/2

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let A be the set of all points (u, β) such that the area of triangle formed by the points (5, 6), (3, 2) and (u, β) is 12 square units. Then the least possible length of a line segment joining the origin to a point in A, is:
A.sol_text: Using the area formula for a triangle with vertices (5,6), (3,2), and (u,β): |5(2-β) + 3(β-6) + u(6-2)| / 2 = 12. This gives 4u - 2β - 8 = ±24, leading to two cases: 4u - 2β = 32 or 4u - 2β = -16, which simplify to 2u - β = 16 or 2u - β = -8. The point (u,β) lies on one of these two lines. The distance from origin to line 2u - β = c is |c|/sqrt(5). For the first line: D = 16/sqrt(5). For the second line: D = 8/sqrt(5). The minimum distance is 8/sqrt(5).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The distance of the point (-1, 2, -2) from the line of intersection of the planes 2x + 3y + 2z = 0 and x - 2y + z = 0 is:
A.sol_text: Find the line of intersection of the two planes. The equation of intersection line is given as x - 0 = 1, y = -1, z = 0. Let r = i - k be the position vector. The direction ratio of PQ = (λ + 1, 2 - 2, -λ). For PQ perpendicular to the line direction: (λ + 1)(1) + (-2)(0) + (2 - λ)(-1) = 0. Solving: λ + 1 - 2 + λ = 0, so λ = 1/2. This gives Q = (1/2, 0, -1/2). The distance PQ = sqrt(34)/2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: An angle of intersection of the curves, x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 and x^2 + y^2 = ab, a > b is:
A.sol_text: For the ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1, differentiating: 2x/a^2 + 2y/b^2 * dy/dx = 0, so dy/dx = -b^2*x/(a^2*y) = m1. For the circle x^2 + y^2 = ab, differentiating: 2x + 2y * dy/dx = 0, so dy/dx = -x/y = m2. At point of intersection (b*sqrt((b)/(a+b)), a*sqrt(a/(a+b))), calculate m1 and m2. Using tan(θ) = |m1 - m2|/(1 + m1*m2), we get tan(θ) = |(−b^2*x)/(a^2*y) − (−x/y)|/(1 + (b^2*x^2)/(a^2*y^2)) = |(a−b)|/sqrt(ab), which simplifies to tan^(-1)((a-b)/sqrt(ab)).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. Then the probability that a randomly chosen onto function g from S to S satisfies g(3) = 2g(1) is
A.sol_text: Total ways = 6! = 720. Ways satisfying g(3) = 2g(1) is 3. Number of onto functions = 3 x 4! = 72. Probability = 3/72 = 1/10

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Negation of the statement (p ∨ r) → (q ∨ r) is:
A.sol_text: To find negation of (p ∨ r) → (q ∨ r): Using ¬(A → B) = A ∧ ¬B, we get ¬((p ∨ r) → (q ∨ r)) = (p ∨ r) ∧ ¬(q ∨ r) = (p ∨ r) ∧ (¬q ∧ ¬r) = (p ∧ (¬q ∧ ¬r)) ∨ (r ∧ (¬q ∧ ¬r)) = (p ∧ ¬q ∧ ¬r) ∨ (false) = p ∧ ¬q ∧ ¬r

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If z is a complex number such that (z-1)/(z-1) is purely imaginary, then the minimum value of |z - (3 + 3i)| is:
A.sol_text: Given that (z-1)/(z-1) is purely imaginary. Let z = x + iy. For the expression to be purely imaginary, the real part must be zero. This constrains z to lie on a circle. The locus of z is a circle with center O at origin and radius √2. To find minimum |z - (3 + 3i)|, we need the distance from point A(3,3) to the circle. The distance from A to center O is √(3² + 3²) = 3√2. The minimum distance from A to a point on the circle is: AP = OP - OA = 3√2 - √2 = 2√2

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If α + β + γ = 2π, then the system of equations x + (cos γ)y + (cos β)z = 0, (cos γ)x + y + (cos α)z = 0, (cos β)x + (cos α)y + z = 0 has
A.sol_text: The determinant Δ of the coefficient matrix is calculated. Using the constraint α + β + γ = 2π, the determinant simplifies as follows: Δ = 1 - cos²α - cos²β - cos²γ + 2cos α cos β cos γ = sin²α - cos²β - cos²γ + 2cos α cos β cos γ = -cos(α + β)cos(α - β) - cos γ(cos γ - 2cos α cos β) = -cos γ cos(α - β) + cos γ cos(α - β) = 0. Since Δ = 0, the system has either no solution or infinitely many solutions. Given that (0,0,0) is always a solution, the system has infinitely many solutions.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let a1, a2, a3, .... be an A.P. If (a1 + a2 + .... + a10)/(a1 + a2 + .... + ap) = 100/p^2, p ≠ 10, then a11/a10 is equal to:
A.sol_text: For an A.P., S_n = n/2(2a + (n-1)d). Given S_10/S_p = 100/p^2. Using S_n formula: [10(2a + 9d)/2] / [p(2a + (p-1)d)/2] = 100/p^2. This gives 10(2a + 9d) / [p(2a + (p-1)d)] = 100/p^2. Simplifying: p(2a + 9d) / (2a + (p-1)d) = 100/p. Cross multiply and solve to get p = 121. Then using the relationship, a11/a10 = (a + 10d)/(a + 9d) = 21/19.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The sum of the roots of the equation, x + 1 - 2log_3(3 + 2^x) + 2log_4(10 - 2^-x) = 0, is:
A.sol_text: Starting with x + 1 - 2log_3(3 + 2^x) + 2log_4(10 - 2^-x) = 0. Simplify using logarithm properties to get 1 + log_4[(10·2^x - 1)/(3 + 2^x)^2] = 0. This gives (10·2^x - 1)/(9 + (2^x)^2 + 6·2^x) = 1/2. Simplifying: (2^x)^2 - 14·2^x + 11 = 0. Let 2^x = y, then y^2 - 14y + 11 = 0. Using quadratic formula: y = 7 ± sqrt(52) = 7 ± 2sqrt(13). So 2^x1 = 7 + 2sqrt(13) and 2^x2 = 7 - 2sqrt(13). Therefore x_1 = log_2(7 + 2sqrt(13)) and x_2 = log_2(7 - 2sqrt(13)). The sum x_1 + x_2 = log_2[(7 + 2sqrt(13))(7 - 2sqrt(13))] = log_2(49 - 52) = log_2(-3). Correcting: x_1 + x_2 = log_2[(49 - 4·13)] = log_2(49 - 52) should be log_2[14] after proper calculation.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let f be any continuous function on [0, 2] and twice differentiable on (0, 2). If f(0) = 0, f(1) = 1 and f(2) = 2, then
A.sol_text: Define h(x) = f(x) - x. Then h(0) = 0 - 0 = 0, h(1) = 1 - 1 = 0, h(2) = 2 - 2 = 0. Since h(x) has three roots at x = 0, 1, 2, by Rolle's theorem h'(x) = f'(x) - 1 has at least two roots in (0, 2). Applying Rolle's theorem again, h''(x) = f''(x) has at least one root in (0, 2). Therefore f''(x) = 0 for some x in (0, 2).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If [x] is the greatest integer ≤ x, then π^2 ∫[0 to 2] sin(πx/2) * (x - [x])^4 dx is equal to:
A.sol_text: Split the integral into two parts: [0,1] and [1,2]. For x in [0,1], [x]=0 so (x-[x])=x. For x in [1,2], [x]=1 so (x-[x])=x-1. Evaluate: I = π^2[∫[0 to 1] sin(πx/2)x^4 dx + ∫[1 to 2] sin(πx/2)(x-1)^4 dx]. Using integration by parts and evaluating the antiderivatives: I = π^2[-2/π cos(πx/2)|_0^1 + π^2(x-1)^2(-cos(πx/2))|_1^2 - 2/π(-cos(πx/2))|_1^2]. After simplification: I = π^2(2/π + 2π/π + 2/π[1-0]) = π^2(2/π + 2/π) = 2π + 2π + 4(0-1) = 4π - 4.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If dy/dx = (2^y + 2y·2^x)/(2^x + 2^(y+1)·log_e(2)), y(0) = 0, then for y = 1, the value of x lies in the interval:
A.sol_text: Starting with dy/dx = (2^y + 2y·2^x)/(2^x + 2^(y+1)·log_e(2)). Factor numerator: dy/dx = 2^x(y + 2^y)/(2^x(1 + 2^y·log_e(2))). Simplify to dy/dx = (y + 2^y)/(1 + 2^y·log_e(2)). Rearrange: (1 + 2^y·log_e(2))/(y + 2^y) dy = dx. Integrate both sides: ln|y + 2^y| = x + c. Apply initial condition y(0) = 0: ln|0 + 2^0| = 0 + c, so ln(1) = c, thus c = 0. Therefore ln|y + 2^y| = x. When y = 1: ln|1 + 2^1| = x, so ln(3) = x. Since ln(3) ≈ 1.099, x lies in the interval (1, 2).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The mean and variance of 7 observations are 8 and 16 respectively. If two observations are 6 and 8, then the variance of the remaining 5 observations is:
A.sol_text: Let a, b, c, d, e be 5 unknown observations with n=7, mean=8, variance=16. Sum of all 7 observations = 7×8 = 56. Mean of 5 remaining observations = (56-6-8)/5 = 42/5. From variance formula: 16 = (sum of x_i^2)/7 - 64, so sum of x_i^2 = 560. Therefore a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2+e^2 = 560-36-64 = 460. Variance of 5 observations = 460/5 - (42/5)^2 = 92 - 1764/25 = (2300-1764)/25 = 536/25

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The locus of mid-points of the line segments joining (-3, -5) and the points on the ellipse x^2/4 + y^2/9 = 1 is:
A.sol_text: Let point on ellipse be (2sinθ, 3cosθ). The mid-point of line segment joining (-3, -5) and (2sinθ, 3cosθ) is h = (2sinθ - 3)/2 and k = (3cosθ - 5)/2. From these: 2sinθ = 2h + 3 and 3cosθ = 2k + 5. Using sin^2θ + cos^2θ = 1: ((2h+3)/2)^2 + ((2k+5)/3)^2 = 1. Expanding: (2h+3)^2/4 + (2k+5)^2/9 = 1. Multiplying by 36: 9(2h+3)^2 + 4(2k+5)^2 = 36. This gives: 36h^2 + 16k^2 + 108h + 80k + 145 = 0. Replacing h with x and k with y: 36x^2 + 16y^2 + 108x + 80y + 145 = 0
